title: Add adventure module schema and typed records
description:
Add an initial adventure module schema and typed record model for immutable authored scenario content.

The schema represents adventure module source only - the authored scenario as written. It must not contain campaign-specific progress fields. Authored elements such as objectives, secrets, scenes, and clocks/threats are modeled as definitions of what is possible in the scenario; whether any of them has been completed, revealed, or advanced is campaign instance state recorded by the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding (eshyra-eh54.4), not by the module record.

The schema should support a small dungeon/adventure module without assuming every module is a linear script. It should support keyed locations, scenes, hooks, NPC roles, encounters, secrets, objectives, treasure, clocks or threats, exits/transitions, and endings.

The first version should be intentionally conservative. The goal is to create a stable destination for starter module content and runtime integration, not to model every possible published adventure format.
design:
Suggested initial concepts (authored source only):

AdventureModule
- id
- title
- summary
- intendedLevels
- intendedPartySize
- rulesetRefs
- settingCompatibility
- startingSituation
- hooks
- locations
- scenes
- npcs
- encounters
- treasure
- secrets
- objectives
- clocksOrThreats
- randomTables
- milestones
- endingStates
- provenance
- license

Important modeling constraint (ADR 0012):

Authored module truth and runtime campaign truth must remain separate. The module record is immutable authored scenario source. For example, the module may define that a sealed shrine lies under the old mill. Whether the players found it, destroyed the mill, bypassed the shrine, or changed the situation is recorded in campaign instance state (the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding), never on the module record. Objectives/secrets/clocks here are definitions of possibilities, not progress flags.
acceptance_criteria:
- A typed adventure module root record exists, representing immutable authored scenario source.
- Module records include stable ids, title/name fields, summary/description fields, tags or categorization where useful, and provenance/license metadata.
- Initial child concepts are represented for hooks, locations, scenes, NPCs, encounters, secrets, objectives, treasure/rewards, clocks/threats, random tables if already supported by existing table concepts, and ending states - all as authored definitions, not progress.
- The schema contains no campaign-specific progress/status fields (no "visited", "revealed", or "completed" flags); progress lives in campaign instance state (eshyra-eh54.4).
- Module records can reference rules-pack content such as creatures, equipment, magic items, rules, actions, and tables without copying mechanical truth into the module.
- Module records can reference compatible campaign-template/setting ids or locations when applicable.
- Validation tests cover at least one small valid module fixture and several broken-reference failures.
- The schema does not mutate or extend SRD rules-pack records to store adventure-specific content.
